description: O Alpha Explorer é um museu interativo dentro do Roblox que ensina crianças e jovens sobre os equipamentos que a NASA enviou ao espaço. O jogador pilota uma nave, enfrenta desafios para recuperar partes da Voyager, do Lunar Roving e do Opportunity e as leva de volta ao museu. A cada recuperação, descobre a história da missão, guiado por Margaret Hamilton, engenheira de software do programa Apollo. Gratuito e acessível pelo celular, leva o conhecimento espacial para onde o público já está.
summary:
What we developed: Alpha Explorer is an interactive space museum within Roblox. The player pilots a ship, faces challenges recovering parts of Voyager, Lunar Roving, and Opportunity, and takes them back to the museum. With each recovery, you learn the story of the mission, guided by Margaret Hamilton, software engineer for the Apollo program.

How the challenge is approached: Many children and young people are unaware of the equipment NASA left in space and what it taught humanity, because this knowledge is dispersed across technical websites, almost always in English. Instead of requiring the public to search for information, we take the content to a platform where it already is, free of charge and accessible via mobile phone.

Why it matters: According to LEGO and the Harris Poll, 86% of children aged 8 to 12 are interested in space exploration and 90% want to learn more. Alpha Explorer turns this interest into learning, sparking curiosity about the science and history of space exploration.
details: Alpha Explorer is an interactive space museum within Roblox that teaches children and young people about the equipment NASA has sent into space. The player starts at the museum, where the exhibits are still empty, and pilots a ship to the location of each piece of equipment: Voyager in interstellar space; Lunar Roving on the Moon; and Opportunity on Mars. At each location, he faces challenges in recovering parts of the equipment and takes them back to the museum, where they become part of the corresponding exhibition. With each recovery, the player discovers the history of the mission, guided by Margaret Hamilton, software engineer for the Apollo program. The equipment NASA sends into space supports much of what we know about the universe, but many people, including children and young people, are unaware of it because this knowledge is scattered across technical websites, almost always in English, without a simple and accessible path for those just starting out. Instead of requiring the audience to search for information, we take the content to a platform where it is already available, free of charge, in Portuguese and accessible via cell phone, and the player learns by completing missions, not by reading passively. The project is creative for inverting the logic of learning, as knowledge is embedded within a mission, for transforming each piece of recovered equipment into a visible display of the player's progress, and for using a real character from the history of space computing as a guide. The intended impact is to spark curiosity about space exploration and create a starting point for those interested in learning about the history of this equipment. The interest is there: according to LEGO and the Harris Poll, 86% of children aged 8 to 12 are interested in space exploration and 90% want to learn more about it. To develop the project, we used [tools, languages and software that you actually used, for example Roblox Studio and Luau]. When designing the experience, the team considered the target audience (school-age children and young space enthusiasts), accessibility (a free platform available on mobile and with content in Portuguese), the choice of three devices in different environments, which demonstrate different phases of exploration, and Roblox's user base, including in Brazil. As a next step, we will publish the MVP test with players and measure how many complete missions and what they learn about each piece of equipment. With the results, we will add new equipment and missions and enhance the experience.
